sections.overview: Phoenicurus phoenicurus, the Common Redstart, is a migratory Old World flycatcher.
sections.identification: The male has a red tail, orange breast, grey back, black face and white forehead; the female is browner.
sections.habitat: It breeds mainly in open deciduous woodland, including mature woods with clearings and nest cavities.
sections.diet: It feeds chiefly on insects and other invertebrates; berries are also eaten.
sections.behavior: European populations migrate to Africa for winter; the bird often flicks its red tail while perched.
sections.reproduction: It nests in tree holes, wall cavities or nest boxes; the female incubates the eggs.
sections.ecology: As a long-distance migrant, it depends on suitable breeding woodland and African wintering habitat. The Black Redstart, Phoenicurus ochruros, is darker and often uses rocky or urban habitats.
sections.conservation: The LPO reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern.
